question: A product team compares two Claude-drafted release notes for the same feature, one for a public changelog and one for an internal engineering wiki. What is a key factor to check for each draft's fit?
options: A) Whether the public draft includes internal ticket numbers so support staff can reference them
B) Whether the internal draft is written with the same marketing tone as the public changelog
C) Whether both drafts are published to the same location so all readers see identical content
D) Whether the public draft avoids internal codenames and detail that the engineering draft can include
correct_answers: D) Whether the public draft avoids internal codenames and detail that the engineering draft can include
explanations: Incorrect. Internal ticket numbers are meaningful to engineers but are not something a general public audience needs or can act on.
Incorrect. A marketing tone suits the public draft but is not a meaningful fit for an internal wiki meant for precise technical reference.
Incorrect. Publishing both drafts to the same location defeats the purpose of tailoring one for public users and one for internal engineers.
Correct. A public changelog should be free of internal codenames and implementation detail, while the internal wiki draft can appropriately retain that detail for engineers.
